proposal.summary: The request was an AI apology-reply assistant (CL-01), but the evidence points to a different problem. CHG-77 turned idempotency-key enforcement off on 2026-09-09 with no rollback (E-01), so timeout retries became real second captures (E-02, E-03), and double-charge tickets rose from about 10 to about 300 per week (E-04). The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: the proposed fix is to re-enable enforcement, but it still needs SH-OPS runtime confirmation (E-07, K-GW), is untested, and several items remain open.
key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1): enforcement was off after CHG-77 (E-01), so gateway timeout retries on H-CAPTURE went out without keys and the PSP no longer dropped them (E-02, E-03).

Duplicate orders were 0 on 09-07 and 09-08, then 118 on 09-09 and 124 on 09-10, matching the daily retry counts of about 120 (E-02). All 242 duplicates were keyless timeout retries, with none from other paths (E-03).
From 09-01 to 09-08, 238 keyed retries were all deduplicated by the PSP (E-03). So the duplication is on the shop side, and H-PSP-SIDE-DUPLICATION was rejected.

Tickets rose from 9 and 11 in W35 and W36 to 288 and 301 in W37 and W38, with orders steady (E-04). H-CS-REPLY-GAP was rejected: SH-CS's view (E-06) is only a claim about the complaint queue, and the evidence contradicts it.
H-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED is CONFIRMED. SH-PAY's account (E-05) agrees with the tool records, but it is non-authoritative and adds nothing the records do not already show.

Release scope: propose re-enabling enforcement on gateway-config (SR-REENABLE-IDEMPOTENCY), verify retry keys in the PSP log, and monitor the ticket trend. The re-enable is only a proposal: SH-OPS must confirm it at runtime under K-GW (E-07), and its plan item W-WI-REENABLE is still PENDING.

Refund scope (U-REFUND-SCOPE) was resolved via E-08, which shows 4 orders with 2 captures and no refund: O-90211, O-90244, O-90302, O-90318. The count of 4 looks low against 242 duplicates, and refunds are still needed (A-REFUND-NEEDED).
The release decision has no holds. The DEFINE gate was CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred items tracked as VOBs and the one blocking VOB (VOB-U-REFUND-SCOPE) resolved.
limitations_explained: The fix is untested (A-FIX-EFFECTIVE). The prediction that duplicates fall to 0 while retries stay near 120 per day has not yet been checked.
The 7-day duplicate window (SC-1) and the 2-week ticket window (SC-3) are longer than the remaining time, so they can only be verified after release.

Customers already double-charged still need refunds or reversals (U-REFUND-SCOPE, A-REFUND-NEEDED). The ledger shows only 4 unrefunded orders (E-08), which looks low against 242 duplicates, so the refund scope is only partly answered.
The original capture latency problem may return once enforcement is on, and it is unknown whether it was ever resolved (U-LATENCY-ORIGINAL).
Ticket counts may miss affected customers who never complained (U-METRIC-VALIDITY).
H-CAPTURE delivery and semantic validity are unknown, and the completeness of the PSP log, config audit log and ticket data assets is marked UNKNOWN.

The change-process fix is not done: SR-TEMP-CHANGE-GOVERNANCE (an expiry date and a named owner for 'temporary' gateway changes, plus an alert when idempotency is off). Until it is, a similar temporary change could recur.
gateway-config tool health is UNKNOWN. The re-enable also depends on SH-OPS runtime confirmation, which has not been recorded.
